items.title: Supreme Court laments lawyer blaming client for AI-generated fake judgments
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently criticised an advocate-on-record (AoR) for attempting to blame litigants after a compilation of judgments submitted before it was alleged to contain non-existent decisions generated using artificial intelligence (AI). [Deepak Raheja v. Omkara] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih observed that the lawyer had attempted to shift responsibility onto the appellants while feigning ignorance of the contents of the compilation. The Court made the observations in a judgment delivered on October 15 while dismissing appeals challenging insolvency proceedings against two companies operating luxury hotels in Bengaluru and Pune. " Before parting, we wish to advert to an undesirable incident that transpired in course of hearing. On behalf of the appellants, a compilation of judgments was placed on record to which the respondents raised immediate serious objection. According to them, the compilation was replete with AI generated non-existent judgments ," the Court recorded. Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih The Bench noted that when questioned about the compilation, the AoR attempted to place the entire responsibility on the appellants. Senior counsel appearing for the appellants subsequently accepted responsibility and sought forgiveness on their behalf. The respondents had also argued that the appellants should not be heard on merits because of their conduct in placing the disputed compilation before the Court. However, the Bench proceeded to hear the appeals while keeping the respondents' objection open. The Court initially proposed imposing exemplary costs on the appellants over the incident. State of Bihar ]. Justice Sandeep Kumar held that in the absence of any overt act towards penetration, such acts fall short of Section 376/511 ( rape/attempt to rape ) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC). Consequently, the High Court set aside the four-year rigorous imprisonment awarded to the accused, one Md Ainul Haque, under Sections 376/511 IPC, reducing his substantive sentence to the period of about two and a half months already spent in custody. It, however, convicted him under Section 354 IPC ( outraging modesty ) and directed him to pay a fine of ₹25,000, ordering the entire amount to be handed over to the victim as compensation. items.title: CADRE ODR appoints Jonathan Rodrigues as Head of Mediation Services
items.summary: CADRE ODR has appointed Jonathan Rodrigues as Head of Mediation Services. Rodrigues will head CADRE ODR’s Mediation Services vertical. He will build and scale an ecosystem, interweaving technology, professional mediation practice and institutional quality standards, that first-time users can navigate with ease and that businesses and institutions can rely on. Rodrigues has more than a decade of mediation practice, advocacy and education in India and internationally. A lawyer by training, he also holds a bachelor’s degree in psychology and an LL.M. in Mediation and Conflict Resolution from the University of Strathclyde, Glasgow. In 2015 he founded The PACT, a mediation institute, where he will continue his advocacy and education work. His appointment brings together his depth in mediation practice with CADRE ODR’s experience in building scalable online dispute resolution technology and processes. This is the first leadership role in an Indian ODR company dedicated to process-driven online mediation. On his appointment, Rodrigues said, “Mediation - everyone loves the idea of it, yet no one seems to have figured out how to make it work as a sustainable practice. I believe the time for that is now. Our objective at CADRE ODR is to build mediation services that are simple enough for a first-time user, credible enough for businesses and institutions, and sophisticated enough to serve complex disputes. Technology can make mediation more accessible; professional standards will make it trusted.” Mediation in an online or virtual context for low-value disputes has often been seen with distrust and pessimism. “I am a sceptic myself,” said Rodrigues, “as the challenge lies in balancing international best practices in mediation, local laws, industry norms – and, what the clients want. However, with an agile engineering team, an accountable institutional framework, we can make mediation an affordable and accessible service, no matter the monetary value of the dispute.” Kanchan Gupta , Co-Founder and CEO, CADRE ODR, said, “There is strong institutional support for mediation, in India and globally, but access to trusted, user-centric mediation is still lacking. items.title: IP ownership in GCCs: Drafting, assignments, transfer pricing considerations and protection strategy
items.summary: Where a global capability centre (“GCC”) undertakes research and development for the multinational group that owns it (“Multinational Group”), ownership of the resulting intellectual property (“IP”) needs to be structured carefully, as the law does not treat all IP as a single category, nor in the same manner in all jurisdictions. For example, in India copyright in an employee’s work vests in the employer by statute, but an employee’s invention remains with the inventor unless assigned in writing. The procedure for transferring each type of IP may also differ. This, along with the intended role and value of the IP to the Multinational Group, should be considered so that the IP is secured, ownership suits the group’s operations, and the arrangement is tax compliant and efficient. A group planning to set up a GCC should settle its IP strategy first. While this article focuses on IP in India, the principles are largely universal. We have dealt mainly with copyright and patents, as these are most likely to arise in a GCC’s work, though the same approach applies to other IP. Clarifying and documenting ownership Stakeholders may agree in principle that a GCC-created IP will be owned (i) by the GCC, (ii) by the Multinational Group from inception, or (iii) by the GCC initially, to be transferred to the Multinational Group later. Since each type of IP is governed by different legislation, how creation and ownership are documented, including with employees and consultants, is critical. Section 17(c) of the Copyright Act, 1957 (“Copyright Act”) vests copyright in a work created by a GCC’s employees in the course of their service in the GCC, so the Multinational Group cannot own that copyright from inception unless it can be treated as a commissioned work, which may not always be possible. An onward transfer is therefore necessary. Section 19 requires the assignment to identify the work and specify the rights assigned, the duration, the territorial extent and the royalty or other consideration payable. If duration and territory are not stated, Sections 19(5) and 19(6) limit them to five years and India. Section 19(4) deems an assignment to have lapsed for rights not exercised within one year, unless the assignment provides otherwise. Authors also retain moral rights of paternity and integrity under Section 57, so the GCC’s employment, consultancy and vendor agreements should expressly waive these to reduce the risk of future claims. items.title: J&K High Court's Ladakh bench to be inaugurated soon; will hear cases from October 21
items.summary: In a major development, the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court's newly constituted Ladakh bench will be inaugurated soon in Leh. Union government had approved establishment of Ladakh bench for the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh in August this year. Following the decision, the High Court on October 5 selected Leh as the place for holding sittings of the High Court in the Union Territory of Ladakh. In the latest, the High Court has identified a total of 75 cases for listing before the bench in Leh. "75 cases pertaining to the Ladakh Division, pending disposal in the Srinagar Wing, have been identified for listing thereof before the newly created Ladakh Bench in connection with its forthcoming inauguration. The dates of hearing of the aforesaid cases have been updated/ preponed to align with the scheduled inaugural hearing of the cases before the Ladakh Bench," the Registrar Judicial said in a notification. The cases have been listed for hearing on October 21, 22 and 23 – indicating that the inauguration will take place in the next few days. Before the establishment of the Ladakh bench, the High Court had two benches at Srinagar and Jammu. Ladakh bench will be part of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, as it currently serves both Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Ladakh was carved out as a separate Union Territory in 2019 following the reorganisation of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir. The decision to establish a bench in Ladakh is aimed at bringing High Court services closer to litigants in Ladakh, where geographical distances can make access to judicial institutions more difficult.

items.title: Vijay Mallya's "flamboyant lifestyle" coming in the way of settling bank claims: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday opined that former Kingfisher Airlines promoter Vijay Mallya’s “flamboyant lifestyle” appears to be hindering the closure of loan recovery proceedings pending against the now-defunct airline [ Diageo Holdings Netherlands B V & others Vs SBI & others ]. A Division Bench of Justice DK Singh and Justice T M Nadaf made the observation while granting relief to Diageo Holdings Netherlands BV in a dispute concerning shares held by Vijay Mallya in United Breweries Limited (UBL), which were pledged in connection with a loan. The Court held that Diageo's claim ranked higher than the entitlement of the banks to these shares. Notably, the Court also observed that the banks had already recovered assets worth ₹14,131.6 crore against the ₹6,203-crore loan given to Kingfisher Airlines. The Court, therefore, held that the banks were not justified in staking a claim over UBL shares as well. " When the Consortium of Banks’ claim for their dues against the loan of INR 6,203 crores has got almost settled by making recovery of assets worth more than INR 14,131.6 crores, there would be no justification for their claim over the UBL shares," the Court held. It went on to observe that Mallya's extravagant lifestyle appears to be the reason why the loan dispute with the banks is yet to be settled. "More than anything else, we are also of the view that it is Dr. Vijay Mallya’s flamboyant lifestyle, excessive personal indulgence and his personal vanity are coming in the way of giving quietus to the claims of the Consortium of Banks against the loan of INR 6,203 crores advanced to the defunct Kingfisher Airlines Ltd," the Court observed. The Bench added that it is up to the bank consortium and the government to close the loan recovery proceedings now. "It is for the Consortium of Banks and the Government of India to give quietus to the proceedings when INR 14,131.6 crores worth of assets have been restored to the Consortium of Banks against their loan of INR 6,203 crores," it said. items.title: Mini Cooper car crash could have been averted: Kerala HC grills State for poor action against speeding vehicles
items.summary: The Kerala High Court today observed that the recently Mini Cooper car crash tragedy, which killed three, could have be averted had the State been proactive to taking action against speeding and reckless vehicle drivers [ Suo Motu v The Chief Secretary and ors and connected cases ]. The car collision took place near the Cochin International Airport (CIAL), Ernakulam last weekend, when a speeding Mini Cooper driven by a 19-year-old had rammed into a scooter, killing three youths. A Division Bench of Justice Raja Vijayaraghavan V and Justice KV Jayakumar referred to this incident today while hearing a case concerning road safety. " This boy was riding at 200 kilometres per hour and your AI camera has spotted it. There should be some method by which you should stop it," the Bench said, addressing the State's counsel. The Court added that a proper system to track and report speeding vehicles could have prevented the fatal collision. " If such an action was taken such an accident would not have happened, " the Judge remarked. Justice Raja Vijayaraghavan V and Justice KV Jayakumar The Court asked why the existing traffic monitoring technology was not being effectively used to identify such speeding vehicles and prevent accidents. " None of these people (driving vehicles at high speeds) have the capability to control these vehicles. If a vehicle is going at 100 kilometres per hour, even if the driver applies the brakes, it will not stop immediately...If a particular person drives at 220 kilometres per hour, will you inform them? Is there any module for that? " Justice Vijayaraghavan remarked. The Court proceeded to seek details of over-speeding violations detected during the past two months. The Bench specifically sought information on vehicles travelling above 150 km/h, as well as details on whether the violations had been reported to the authorities concerned and whether any action had been taken. Justice Vijayaraghavan also raised concerns about the risk posed by high-performance cars when they are driven at dangerously high speeds on roads in Ernakulam, particularly after midnight. " We are asking you to set up some sort of expert management team who can devise a better method, because speed should not be an incentive for the drivers, " the Judge remarked. Justice Jayakumar added that the authorities must propose effective measures to address these concerns. " We want practical solutions on how to tackle this issue, not a formal counter, " he said. items.title: Supreme Court grants relief to journalist booked in SC/ST case after she accused cop of sexual harassment
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday granted interim protection to a journalist booked for making casteist remarks against Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat, days after she accused the police officer of sexually harassing her while she was covering the ongoing Delhi protests. items.title: Actor Imran Khan to move Bombay High Court against notice to leave India after protests against CEC
items.summary: Bollywood actor Imran Khan will approach the Bombay High Court challenging the notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) which directs him to leave the country by October 28 for allegedly violating the Foreigners Act. Once the plea is filed, it will be moved for an urgent hearing. The plea is likely to be heard by the division bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna . Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait Sethna Khan is being represented by advocates Zulfiquar Memon, Parvez Memon and Chirag Naik from MZM Legal LLP. The administrative action follows Khan’s detention on October 10 during a demonstration at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. After the demonstration, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Kirit Somaiya lodged a complaint at the Gamdevi police station. He alleged that the actor, a United States (US) citizen, breached the Foreigners Act by participating in the political morcha. The Gamdevi police subsequently forwarded the complaint to the FRRO for necessary action. The immigration authority acted on the complaint and served an expulsion notice to the actor. According to reports , the FRRO directive cited his US citizenship and flagged his participation in the demonstration as an infraction of immigration and foreigners regulations. Khan has been ordered to leave the territory of India on or before October 28. Khan is an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) cardholder. While the 2005 OCI scheme grants foreign nationals of Indian origin a lifelong visa to visit and reside in India, it does not confer Indian citizenship or political privileges such as voting or contesting elections. Under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, the Central government has the authority to direct a foreigner to “not remain in India or in any specified area therein".

Pertinently, the Delhi Police on October 13 told the Delhi High Court that the decision was taken based on the Supreme Court's order of October 9. However, the Central government today denied the same. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi questioned the Centre, "[Was it de-notified] Because of some oral observations of the Court, or was there an application of mind with regard to the site and its efficacy in being used as a common protest site?" CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union, replied, "The Court's judgment is not the basis of the decision. The committee was constituted much before. The committee has given a detailed report." SG Tushar Mehta Senior Advocate Mukta Gupta , appearing for the petitioner, stressed on the fundamental rights of citizens to protest peacefully. "The fundamental right of a citizen to carry out a protest cannot be scuttled because this Court has already ruled in Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan that the place has to be somewhere near where protesters can be heard. items.title: Kerala High Court suspends ex-DGP Tomin Thachankary's four-year jail sentence in DA case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Thursday suspended the 4-year-jail sentence of former Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin Thachankary in a disproportionate assets case [ Tomin J Thachakary v State of Kerala ]. Justice A Badharudeen pronounced the order on an application filed by Thachankary seeking suspension of his jail sentence until the High Court decides his appeal challenging the conviction. While allowing Thachankary's plea, the Court observed that, prima facie there was no error in the vigilance court's finding that he had acquired assets disproportion to his known income. However, considering that the sentence imposed on him was only four years, the Court held that it could be suspended by imposing appropriate conditions. It, thus, directed him to deposit 75% of the ₹30.84 lakh fine imposed by the vigilance court before he could be released on bail and to execute a bail bond of ₹5 lakh with two sureties within a further period of one week after depositing the fine amount. A subsequent probe by the vigilance revealed that Thachankary had acquired assets worth over ₹64 lakh between 2003 and 2007. Senior counsel B Raman Pillai, appearing for Thachankary, argued that the trial court's findings were illegal and that the prosecution's evidence was insufficient to establish the alleged offence. items.title: Bark, bite or let sleeping dogs lie?
items.summary: Watchdog of the Constitution. Apex Ombudsman. Sentinel on the qui vive. Even as its monikers get more obscure, the role of the Supreme Court of India as the final protector of our rights has always been clear. That the Court has not always covered itself in glory while guarding the house we live in is, in its own words, a shame that deserves to be buried ten fathoms deep . Amidst reluctant whispers of the 'E' word (Emergency Lite, if you will) today, its ears surely must prick up. The mantle that rests on its shoulders, its own former members would say, has never weighed heavier in recent times than now. On October 15, the apex watchdog will hear a number of matters on protests related to the functioning of the Election Commission of India (ECI), the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, voter deletions and the State's quelling of those same protests. At stake are a host of rights guaranteed under the Constitution of India, the very document the Supreme Court was formed to protect. There is an eternal question the Supreme Court has grappled with over the course of its history - when and to what extent should it interfere in executive functioning? The answers are as diverse as the members who have made up the institution. Some courts have acted to executive overreach with haste, others reposed faith in the assurances of the government and others still stayed their hands till there was nothing left to safeguard. The more important question is: what does the Court do when the executive fails to adhere to its orders and judgments in true spirit? Recent history shows more than one instance of this trend – all related to the issues that will come up before the Court on Thursday. Don’t beware of watchdog The Court’s own jurisprudence on a number of these issues is already clear. In Anoop Baranwal , it laid down the principle that appointments to the ECI must be insulated from executive interference. The subsequently enacted Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 flies in the face of this principle. It also forms the basis of this whole fiasco – the appointment of a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) whose independence has been called into question. items.title: Delhi court issues fresh summons to YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday issued fresh summons against Youtuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case filed by Vikas Sankrityayan, alias Vikas Pandey. On October 12, Judicial Magistrate Rahul Jain from Saket Court allowed an application seeking early hearing and the issuance of dasti (by hand) summons against Rathee. Advocate Samaksh Sharma for the complainant argued that summons had remained unserved for several years as Rathee primarily resides abroad. items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that it can execute a decree arising from a commercial suit even if the amount sought to be recovered is below its ₹2 crore pecuniary jurisdiction threshold, provided the original suit was within its jurisdiction [Ozone SPA Vs Co-incept] Justice Subramonium Prasad held that a court does not lose its jurisdiction to execute a decree merely because the decretal amount falls below its pecuniary threshold. " The contention that alteration in pecuniary limit of the court which passed the decree would also take away the power of such Court to execute the said decree cannot be accepted ," the Court observed. Justice Subramonium Prasad The ruling came in an execution petition filed by Ozone Spa Private Limited against Co-Incept Hospitality Private Limited and others, seeking enforcement of a ₹1.19 crore decree passed in July 2018. The dispute arose from a franchise agreement executed in December 2013, under which Co-Incept Hospitality was permitted to operate a gym, spa and salon under the Ozone brand at Rajouri Garden in Delhi. Following disputes over royalty payments, Ozone Spa filed a commercial suit seeking recovery of ₹2.53 crore and a permanent injunction. The parties subsequently entered into a settlement agreement in July 2018, based on which the High Court passed a consent decree. Ozone Spa later alleged that the judgment debtors breached the settlement by failing to issue post-dated cheques, defaulting on royalty payments and closing the outlet without notice. One of the judgment debtors challenged the maintainability of the execution petition, arguing that the ₹1.19 crore sought to be recovered was below the ₹2 crore threshold applicable to the High Court's Commercial Division. The High Court rejected the objection. It relied on Sections 37 and 38 of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), which permit a decree to be executed by the court that passed it or by another court to which it is transferred. The Court also referred to earlier Delhi High Court decisions holding that changes in pecuniary jurisdiction do not automatically deprive a court of its power to execute decrees already passed by it. The Court further clarified that Sections 37 and 38 of the CPC apply to decrees passed under the Commercial Courts Act. items.summary: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) has told the Supreme Court that there was no complete ban on metro services on the day of the proposed protests at Jantar Mantar. It said that only 45 of its 303 stations were closed for entry and exit on October 10, after the Supreme Court on October 9 ordered that there shall be no outright prohibition on the movement of metro trains. DMRC Chairperson D Thara has also tendered an "unconditional apology" in an affidavit filed in response to a contempt notice issued on October 11. items.title: NCLAT stays insolvency proceedings against Polycab India over ₹2.78 crore debt
items.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) has stayed insolvency proceedings against cable and wire manufacturer Polycab India Limited over an alleged operational debt of ₹2.78 crore. [Bharat Ajay Jaisinghani v. Asier Metals Pvt. Ltd. & Anr.] NCLAT's principal bench comprising officiating chairperson Justice Yogesh Khanna and technical members Barun Mitra and Ajai Das Mehrotra granted interim relief on October 9 in an appeal filed by Bharat Ajay Jaisinghani, the suspended director of Polycab. The tribunal directed that the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) be kept in abeyance, subject to Polycab depositing the entire claimed amount of ₹2.78 crores. Senior Advocate Arun Kathpalia , appearing for Jaisinghani, submitted that Polycab was ready to deposit the sum without prejudice to its rights and contentions. items.summary: "You ate his ear, how do we replace it?" the Supreme Court asked a man on Wednesday, giving short shrift to his petition for anticipatory bail in an assault case. Injecting a dose of dry judicial wit into the hearing, a Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran made it clear that a litigant accused of chomping off a neighbour's ear during a street clash could hardly expect pre-arrest protection. The matter reached the top court on an appeal challenging a February 2026 order of the Jharkhand High Court, which had refused anticipatory bail to one Rajiv Ranjan Kumar over a violent clash in Ranchi. Kumar's counsel attempted to soften the blow by painting the incident as a routine neighbourhood feud that simply spiralled out of control on a festive night. "It’s a long-simmering dispute between neighbours. It flared up on one night and cross-FIRs were registered. The opposite side managed to get anticipatory bail while I was denied the same. The way it started was, it was the night of Janmashtami, people were celebrating and there was some stone pelting..." the counsel submitted. "Aapne pehle bandook nikali, phir uska kaan pakad liya, aur pura kaan khaa gaye aap. (You first took out a pistol, then held his ear and ate it) And you want anticipatory bail? " the Court remarked. Kaan ka kya karein? (Okay, let the pistol be, what do we do about the ear?) How do we replace it?" the Court quipped. The counsel claimed his client was actually the primary victim of the tussle. A Division Bench of Justices Sanjeev Kumar and MA Chowdhary passed the interim order while hearing the senior advocate’s writ petition against the Tribunal’s order. The Court was hearing a case related to the election dispute between Congress leader TD Rajegowda and BJP candidate DN Jeevaraj. Rajegowda had won the assembly elections from Sringeri assembly constituency in 2023 by a narrow margin of 201 votes. However, the Congress candidate was recently unseated after a recount declared that Jeevaraj had secured more votes. In May, the top court granted Rajegowda relief by directing that he shall remain the Member of Legislative Assembly (MLA) during the pendency of his plea. Today, a bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva expressed surprise after the ECI said that it was unable to trace the video recording of the counting that took place in 2023. "How can the Election Commission of India (ECI) say that it has lost its record? Your whole purpose is to hold an election, and you need to have a document. Where is the question of you saying, ‘Yeah, we are trying to trace it’? You gave it to the elected candidate. There is no custody of records. Whatever you have, produce it on the next date. items.title: J&K High Court says doctors hesitant to perform abortions without court order, aggrieved mothers left at God's mercy
items.summary: The Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court recently observed that doctors refuse to perform abortions even in cases where the procedure is legally permitted under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Act. Justice Mohd Yousuf Wani made the comment while dealing with a case of a woman who, despite serious foetal abnormalities, had to approach the Court for medical termination of pregnancy after doctors refused to perform abortion without judicial order. The Court emphasised that medical practitioners should not unnecessarily avoid attending emergent cases for which statutory directions under the MTP Act and relevant rules are clear. "The registered medical practitioners especially doctors working in the associated hospitals of medical colleges and in other district hospitals do not shoulder their statutory responsibilities in terms of the provisions of Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act, 1971 and the rules of 2003 framed thereunder in justified cases thereby leaving the aggrieved mothers at the mercy of the God who, in search of some solace feel constrained to shoulder further mental agony and burden of approaching the courts of law for legal directions," the Court said. Justice Mohammad Yousuf Wani Under the MTP Act, termination of pregnancy is permitted up to 24 weeks subject to prescribed conditions, while terminations beyond 24 weeks are highly restricted. The Court further said that clause 2-B of Section 3 and clause 1 of Section 5 of the MTP Act clearly reveal that the provisions relating to length of pregnancy do not apply to termination of pregnancy in cases with substantial foetal abnormalities or where abortion is necessary to save the life of the pregnant women. The order was passed on a petition moved by a couple for directions to constitute a medical board for termination of pregnancy in view of detection of serious abnormalities in the foetus at the gestational age of 31 weeks. On September 29, the doctors told the couple that due to the advanced stage of the foetus, the termination cannot be undertaken without the intervention of the High Court. The couple then moved the Court seeking consideration under the statutory framework governing termination beyond the ordinary gestational limit in cases of substantial foetal abnormalities. items.title: “They don't take this seriously?” Supreme Court on Centre's failure to respond to plea for strict age checks at liquor outlets
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday expressed concern over the Union government's failure to appear in the hearing of a plea seeking mandatory age verification at liquor outlets across the country, despite the service of notice [ Community Against Drunken Driving Versus The Union Of India And Ors. ]. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath , Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh heard the matter briefly today, when it noted that no counsel had appeared for the Central government despite service of notice. “Respondent 1 (the Union Government) notice is served. No one is appearing for the Union. It is an important issue. They don't take you seriously?” remarked Justice Nath. "They are not taking the matter seriously," replied the petitioner's counsel. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The Court proceeded to grant the Union government four weeks to file its response. The Bench also said that it would request the Solicitor General of India, Tushar Mehta to appear in the matter. The Court has directed the petitioner to serve a copy of the order on the Solicitor General's office. The matter has been listed next after six weeks. The plea has been filed by a non-profit organisation named Community Against Drunken Driving (CADD). It seeks directions to establish a mandatory age-verification system at liquor shops, bars, pubs and restaurants to prevent underage drinking and curb incidents of drunk driving. The plea highlights the absence of a uniform mechanism to verify the age of people purchasing alcohol. It argued that inadequate checks allow minors to access alcohol and contribute to accidents involving underage drivers allegedly driving under the influence. During Wednesday's hearing, counsel for the petitioner argued that a uniform protocol was necessary because the minimum legal age for purchasing alcohol varied across States. The counsel said that the concern was about the mechanism used to verify a liquor purchaser's age and called on the Union government to harmonise the process. “There should be a protocol mandate for age verification at the first point of sale all over India because you have eight States with minimum age requirement as 25 years, 18 years. items.title: What is your fear? Madras High Court questions State over refusal to permit RSS marches
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Wednesday questioned the Tamil Nadu government's repeated refusal to grant permission for route marches by the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), asking what the State feared from such processions [ Jagadeesan Vs State ]. The Court was hearing a petition challenging police orders refusing permission for RSS marches proposed in October. " What is your fear? Are you fearing.. ." Justice V Lakshminarayanan asked the Tamil Nadu Advocate General. Justice V Lakshminarayanan Advocate General Vijay Narayan explained that permitting the marches would require substantial police deployment at a time when the authorities also had other responsibilities during the festive season. He added that processions could inconvenience members of the public engaged in shopping and other activities. Senior Advocate Vijay Narayan The Court, however, questioned why the State continued to refuse permission despite previous judicial orders allowing RSS processions. " Every year they (RSS) are coming (seeking permission for rallies), every year, court is granting. What is so exceptional for 2026? Has there been any violence so far in their march ?" the Court remarked. Where criminal cases on account of violence, you please tell me," said Justice Lakshminarayanan. The Court also raised concerns about the State's general approach towards citizens seeking to exercise their constitutional rights. " State is looking at citizens as enemies, what to do? " The judge observed that a change in attitude was necessary and that successive governments had been refusing permission for processions. " Whichever government is in power, they are rejecting it, " he remarked. The Court questioned the need for repeated litigation over such permissions. items.title: Calcutta High Court denies bail to ex-minister Sujit Bose in money laundering case
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court has rejected former West Bengal minister Sujit Bose's bail plea in a money laundering case linked to the alleged South Dum Dum municipality recruitment scam [Sujit Bose v. Directorate of Enforcement] Justice Tithankar Ghosh observed that Bose failed to meet the mandatory requirements for bail under Section 45 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA). The Court also observed that no reasonable ground existed to believe that Bose was not guilty and was not likely to commit any other offence while on bail. It added that he cannot be released merely because the prosecution’s complaint stands filed and that the trial court has taken cognizance in the matter. "The Central Bureau of Investigation has also commenced further investigation after informing the Learned Special Court pursuant to receipt of information by the Enforcement Directorate. A vital stage of the investigation is in progress," the Court said in an order passed on October 13. According to the ED, various illegal municipal recruitments were carried out on recommendations received from Bose and other "politically exposed persons". Senior Advocate, Abhishek Manu Singhvi , appearing for Bose, submitted that he always cooperated with the Enforcement Directorate whenever summoned and was only arrested three years after the registration of the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR). He further argued that the delay in arrest itself negates any genuine requirement for custodial interrogation, apprehension of flight risk or possibility of tampering. Additional Solicitor General SV Raju , appearing for the ED alleged that Bose had laundered almost ₹20.40 crore through various accounts, including through his own and his family members'. It was also submitted that seized digital records, recruitment data, property transactions, cash deposits, shareholding arrangements and structured payments establish both generation and laundering of proceeds of crime by the accused. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday came down heavily on the Chhattisgarh High Court, questioning how its judges could be expected to properly assess evidence if they did not understand basic principles of criminal law. A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran made the remarks while hearing a plea challenging a November 2024 judgment of the Chhattisgarh High Court. The High Court order had set aside a man's murder conviction and instead convicted him of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and sentenced him to 10 years in prison instead of life imprisonment. "Just see the pathetic condition of the High Court. The judges don’t know what is Section 304 part I (culpable homicide not amounting to murder involving intention to cause death or likely-fatal injury) and Section 304 Part II IPC (culpable homicide not amounting to murder involving knowledge that the act is likely to cause death, but no such intention)! And you expect the judges to appreciate the evidence!" said the Court. The Bench further criticised the High Court for what it described as a recurring failure to understand basic legal principles. “This is not the first judgement we are coming across. These are all principles of law which law schools teach in the first year of academic session,” said the Court. items.title: PIL in Delhi High Court for crackdown on non-dairy products being sold as paneer
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday sought a response from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the Central and Delhi governments, as well as the Commissioner of Food Safety to a plea seeking action against dairy analogues and non-dairy products being sold or served as paneer in the national capital. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma directed the authorities to file their reply in six weeks. The petitioners also sought interim directions to conduct an enforcement drive against such non-dairy products being sold as paneer. It was submitted that in view of the coming festive season, such action is important. However, the Court said that it was not passing any interim directions for now. Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre, Justice Sanjay Sharma The public interest litigation (PIL) has been filed by a law student named Ridhima Singh and advocate Avlokiteshwar Padmapani Sidharth. It seeks directions to the authorities to crack down on dairy analogues and non-dairy products being sold or served as paneer in the national capital. The petitioners have urged the Court to direct the Delhi government and food safety authorities to undertake regular inspections, sampling and testing of paneer at manufacturing units, wholesale markets, distributors, retail outlets and food service establishments. They have argued that consumers ordering dishes such as paneer tikka, kadai paneer and paneer butter masala ordinarily expect to be served a dairy product and may have no way of knowing whether a non-dairy substitute has been used by a restaurant or cloud kitchen. The plea adds that it does not seek a blanket prohibition on lawful plant-based or dairy analogue products, but seeks action against non-dairy products being passed off as paneer without adequate disclosure. It further relies on measures taken by food safety authorities in Maharashtra and other States to argue that enforcement action can be considered under the existing legal framework without waiting for amendments to regulations. items.title: Property acquired by Catholic priests after joining religious order belongs to society, not legal heirs: Madras High Court
items.summary: The Madras High Court has held that properties acquired by Catholic priests after entering a religious order and undertaking religious vows belong to the religious society concerned and cannot be claimed by their legal heirs merely on the basis of their family relationship [ ABVM Vs Deiva Nayagan ]. A Division Bench of Justices N Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan passed the ruling while allowing appeals filed by a Catholic religious society against a district court order granting succession rights to the relatives of a deceased priest over fixed deposits worth ₹56 lakh. The Court held that the ownership of properties acquired during a priest's religious service must be determined in light of the obligations undertaken by the priest and the circumstances of the property's acquisition. " The legal consequence of such acquisition must therefore be determined in the light of the religious obligations undertaken by him and the institutional character in which those properties were acquired, rather than merely by the fact that the title documents stood in his individual name," the judgment said. Justices Anand Venkatesh and KK Ramakrishnan The Court explained that the concept of a person's "civil death" upon his entering a religious order signifies the person's renunciation of worldly relationships and interests. However, it clarified that civil death does not mean that a priest ceases to exist as a legal person or loses all civil rights. The Bench distinguished between properties acquired before entering a religious order and those acquired subsequently in accordance with the obligations governing the concerned religious order. It held that properties independently inherited from family members cannot automatically be treated as belonging to the religious society. The Court also drew a distinction between diocesan priests and priests belonging to religious orders who have undertaken perpetual vows. It observed that diocesan priests do not, merely by becoming priests, assume the same obligations concerning renunciation of worldly possessions as those entering religious orders. The ruling came in appeals filed by the ABVM Society of the Catholic Apostolate (Pallottines), which claimed entitlement to fixed deposits worth ₹56 lakh left behind by the late Reverend Father Devakumar Arulanantham. items.title: SCBA issues show cause notice to Balraj Malik over face-off with President Pradeep Rai
items.summary: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) has issued a show cause notice to Advocate Balraj Singh Malik over his alleged conduct towards its President and Senior Advocate Pradeep Kumar Rai, asking him to explain why he should not be suspended or expelled from the Association. items.title: Add photos, videos of illegal modifications while uploading accident vehicle reports: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has directed the Motor Vehicles Department (MVD) to ensure that photographs and videos of of illegal modifications to vehicles involved in accidents must be part of the accident reports uploaded on the Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e-DAR) portal [ Suo Motu v Union of India & Ors ]. Justices Anil K Narendran and Muralee Krishna S gave the directions on October 8, 2026, while considering a suo motu case dealing with road safety and unauthorised modification of vehicles in Kerala. " We deem it appropriate to direct (the Transport Commissioner), through the concerned Deputy Transport Commissioners, to ensure that vehicle modification details with photographs and videos of vehicles involved in accidents are uploaded through e-DAR portal (www.irad.parivahan.gov.in), by the concerned inspecting officers, " the Court said. Inspecting officers must upload details of any violation of safety standards that raise the risk of injury to the person hit by or brushing against the bodywork of such vehicles, the Court added. The Court further directed that details uploaded on the online portal should specifically include illegal alterations made to increase the performance of the vehicle's engine and any changes made to the braking system. JUSTICE ANIL K NARENDRAN AND JUSTICE MURALEE KRISHNA S The Court passed the order after noting that the Transport Commissioner had already issued comprehensive instructions on September 17, 2026, to transport officials regarding the inspection of vehicles involved in accidents and the upload of their photos and videos. items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Wednesday refused to grant an interim injunction against the JioStar over its upcoming movie Queen Forever [Phantom Studios v. JioStar India & Ors]. Justice Sandeep Marne declined relief to Phantom Studios, which claimed that the movie was an unauthorised sequel to the 2014 film Queen. A detailed order is awaited. Justice Sandeep Marne Phantom sued JioStar India for ₹250 crore alleging that Queen Forever breaches a 2012 co‑production agreement and a 2022 deed of novation under which Phantom and JioStar (earlier Viacom18) are claimed to be joint and equal owners of all intellectual property and derivative rights in Queen. In the interim application which Justice Marne decided today, Phantom sought an order temporarily barring the defendants from making, releasing, or promoting any sequel or adaptation of the film (including Queen Forever ) without Phantom's written permission until the suit is finally decided. JioStar denied these allegations claiming the new film is not a continuation of the original film. It contended that Phantom had been aware of the project since April 2025 and had already engaged in correspondence with JioStar. The company also pointed out that the film is expected to release later this year. After considering the arguments, the Court today declined to grant any interim injunction. items.title: Jammu and Kashmir High Court makes AIBE mandatory for advocates enrolled since 2009-10
items.summary: The Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently made it mandatory for all advocates enrolled across the Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh since 2009-10 to pass the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) to be entitled to practice law. Although the Bar Council of India (BCI) had made AIBE mandatory for law graduates from 2009-10 onwards, the requirement had not been formally implemented for advocates enrolled with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh. The Jammu and Kashmir High Court has now directed its implementation. A notification to this effect was issued by the High Court's Registrar General MK Sharma on October 10, 2026. The notification lays down that law graduates enrolled as advocates with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, who graduated in the academic year 2009-2010 onwards, must qualify the AIBE if they have not already cleared the examination. Fresh law graduates and advocates enrolled provisionally will be granted an absolute certificate of enrolment only after passing the AIBE and producing the Certificate of Practice (COP) issued by the Bar Council of India within two years. Advocates enrolled with the Bar Council of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh after July 1, 2010, who have already qualified the AIBE, have been directed to submit copies of their Certificates of Practice to the High Court Registry within one month. The decision follows the Full Court's October 8 decision to accept an August 19 recommendation of a Rules Committee to implement Rules 9, 10 and 11 of Chapter III, Part VI of the Bar Council of India Rules concerning the AIBE. Rule 9 of the BCI Rule stipulates that advocates must successfully pass the AIBE to be entitled to practise under Chapter IV of the Advocates Act, 1961. Rule 11 provides for the issuance of the Certificate of Practice to successful candidates. items.title: Homemaker’s household services cannot be ignored in accident compensation merely because she is over 70: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that while determining motor accident compensation, a homemaker’s unpaid household and caregiving services cannot be disregarded merely because she is above 70 years of age [Ganga Devi v Rajesh Kumar & Ors] . Justice Anish Dayal said that the assessment of compensation should not be founded upon stereotypes or assumptions that a person ceases to contribute merely by reason of having attained an advanced age. The Court warned against such prejudices and said that data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. “This Court is conscious that such contributions, particularly those rendered within the household and without monetary remuneration, are often overlooked or undervalued. However, the absence of a monetary consideration cannot operate to the advantage of the tortfeasor or diminish the compensation otherwise payable to the injured claimant,” the Bench ruled. Justice Anish Dayal Delhi High Court Data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. The Court made the observations while allowing an appeal filed by Ganga Devi, who was 74 when a bus accident in February 2019 crushed both her legs. She suffered 74 percent permanent disability in relation to both lower limbs. The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) awarded her ₹14.42 lakh in compensation but denied claims for loss of income and future income. The tribunal reasoned that she was an elderly woman who had never been employed and that there was insufficient evidence of her contribution to household work. However, the Court rejected this approach. It observed that such assumptions risk perpetuating age-based stereotypes, commonly described as ageism. The Court underscored that older people do not merely receive care from younger family members but also continue to provide valuable domestic assistance, including looking after grandchildren. The court noted that unpaid household work has identifiable economic value, as families would otherwise have to spend money on cooking, childcare and other domestic services. items.title: Jailer 2: Nelson-Rajini team up for more of the same, but with less fun
items.summary: Director Nelson Dileepkumar’s Jailer 2 may exhaust you, then lull you into a stupor with its bottomless supply of excesses. Sequels mostly work if the previous film possessed some internal logic to continue from. But while Jailer (2023) was a quirky and fun watch , it was also full of laughable plot holes that didn’t come with enough stakes to set up a worthy second instalment. And now, possibly, a third. In Jailer 2, Rajinikanth returns as ‘Tiger’ Muthuvel Pandian, a retired warden who once terrorised inmates at Tihar jail. The first film established Muthu (a callback to the 1995 Rajini film of the same name) as a man whose influence reaches far beyond that of any prison warden and spans several states. Jailer 2 carries that forward along with his skill to hide in plain sight. Working as a driver for a bumbling small-time thug, Muthu continues his crusade against an idol-smuggling mafia. The film builds up to a face-off between him and Bodhi Kalpak (SJ Suryah). Suryah’s trademark theatrics are a few shades more muted in Jailer 2 , which makes Bodhi one of the more interesting characters. He manages to infuse some comedy into his role, often through his bewilderment at the lengths Muthu is willing to go. It says something about a Kollywood hero if even Suryah’s character is mystified to the point of doubting his nemesis’ stability. As Anirudh’s pounding, screeching score ratchets up and the film flits from one big explosion to the next while sprinkling meagre bits of an actual plot along the way, you’re left wondering what it is that Muthu even wants? items.title: Explainer: Why buying power at Rs 37 per unit has sparked a political storm in Tamil Nadu
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to purchase power for up to Rs 37 per unit has triggered a big political row, prompting criticism over whether it was a result of poor planning or corruption. This is the highest cost of power paid in Tamil Nadu’s history, and is highly unusual for almost any state discom in the country. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government has cited an unexpected high demand amid a prolonged summer due to the El Niño phenomenon as the reason for the high cost. According to the Energy Resources Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar, the state’s peak power demand shot up by almost 30% from around 16,800 MW in October 2025 to nearly 21,700 MW this October – an additional requirement of nearly 5,000 MW. But the El Niño crisis has been felt across India, including the neighbouring south Indian states. Critics have compared the situation with that of Andhra Pradesh to question the lack of prior planning. Andhra Pradesh, too, is facing a surge in demand and had to resort to short-term power procurement deals. However, the state took measures as early as the first week of September. As many critics have pointed out, the Andhra Pradesh Power Coordination Committee (APCC) has also purchased power on a short-term basis for a similar period as Tamil Nadu’s expensive agreement – around 150 MW for a price of Rs 16 to Rs 20 per unit from October 1 to October 31. But this agreement was finalised by September 9. The West Bengal state discom also managed to purchase power on the short term market from October 11 to 19 at Rs 14.5 per unit, the DEEP (Discovery of Efficient Electricity Price) e-bidding web portal of the Union Ministry of Power shows. This agreement too was finalised over a month in advance, by September 1. The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL), however, invited bids to procure additional power of 4,500 MW on a short-term basis for October 12 to 31, only on October 6, a week ahead. The bids accepted are for 2062 MW of power at prices ranging from Rs 32 to Rs 34.5, and another 2001 MW for Rs 33.37 to Rs 37. The highest price of Rs 37 applies to 181 MW. Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar has said that only power from gas plants was available at the time of bidding. TNPDCL officials have said that the fixed charge per unit (regardless of actual power used) in the case of gas plants is only Re 1 per unit, which is much lower than that of coal plants, and would lower the cost in case of any unutilised power. items.summary: Around mid-September, a video on Facebook caught the attention of Bagalkot District Health Officer (DHO) Suvarna Kulkarni. It showed a person in a car outside the house of a woman and another person allegedly carrying equipment and pills used for abortions. The video caught the attention of Suvarna and other health officials as the woman in the video, Kavita Badanavar, was known to them. Kavita Badanavar had been booked twice before in cases regarding illegal medical practice. In one case, she is accused of medically terminating the pregnancy of a woman in Mahalingpur in 2024 despite not being a registered medical practitioner. The woman, a native of Kolhapur, Maharashtra, died. When the video of Kavita surfaced on social media, the district health department decided to look into it. Kannada television media carried visuals from this video . items.title: Fire near Kochi's Kadavumbhagam Synagogue: SIT formed to probe suspected terror links
items.summary: A special investigation team (SIT) has been constituted to conduct a probe into the suspected extremist links in an incident of arson in front of the historic Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Kochi. Kadavumbhagam Synagogue is a Jewish place of worship built around 1549. The arrested youth, Ebin B Paul, had set fire to the signboard of Blossom Nursery kept at the entrance of the narrow lane that leads to the Synagogue. Two civil police officers, who were deputed for the security of Synagogue, have been suspended following the incident. Deputy Commissioner of police, Kochi city, Arun Pavitran will supervise the SIT headed by Assistant Commissioner, Ernakulam Central, Sibi Tom. Accused Ebin, 32, a native of Puthencruz in Ernakulam, was arrested by Ernakulam Central police hours after the fire. The alleged incident happened around 2.30 am on October 12. As per a statement by police, Ebin has set fire to the boards placed at the Blossom Nursery in front of the Synagogue gate. It said that Ebin, who arrived in a blue Ignis car, used petrol to set fire. He left the scene after recording the arson on his mobile phone. As per report, the fire did not cause any damages to the synagogue. The Ernakulam Judicial First class Magistrate court on Thursday, October 15, remanded the accused in five-day custody of the SIT. The defence told the court that the accused was suffering from severe mental health issues and was under psychiatric treatment. Taking this into account, the court asked the investigating team to ensure that the accused gets necessary medicines and care. It also directed the SIT to submit a report within 48 hours regarding the status of his mental condition. Meanwhile police claimed to have collected crucial digital evidence from the accused. “Apart from visuals of the arson, suspected foreign links and communication in various online groups were found.There are indications that the crime was committed as per the direction of an unidentified person, whom Ebin addressed as Boss. Preliminary investigation points to the pattern in which the accused who was assigned targets would commit the arson, record the visuals and receive the payment,” the statement said. Police are looking into the possible use of cryptocurrency for financial transactions. Police said that the communications in the mobile phone of the accused point to various targets, including Jewish religious sites, and communications related to possible attacks on various parts of the country.
